title: 'Pain is nearly orthogonal to fear/negative valence' is an artefact of the estimator as a COSINE statement, but survives as a DISCRIMINATION statement
paper_claim: "If the pain vectors were simply variants of negative valence, they should fall within the negative valence cluster. Instead, the two pain vectors align strongly with each other and remain nearly orthogonal to the main negative-valence directions."
evidence: scripts/x1_geometry.py -> out/x1_geometry_Gemma_2_2B_instruct.txt; gpu_repro/out/baseline_symmetry_{Gemma_2_2B_instruct,Mistral_7B_base}.txt. At Gemma 2 2B instruct L25 the k=5 PCA basis projected out of the pain vector holds 0.801/0.859/0.853/0.756 of the raw fear/negE/negW/bodysens directions but only 0.389 of the raw pain direction (random direction: 0.0022); Mistral 7B base L26, k=7: 0.797/0.839/0.864/0.833. Symmetric constructions: with every direction built vs the neutral mean and denoised on the neutral cloud, S2 x fear +0.696, S2 x negE +0.814 against fear x negE +0.705 - pain is more central to the cluster than fear. With a leave-one-out pooled baseline the control cluster inverts (fear x negE -0.536), so no construction is neutral. Partial cosines on a common basis: pain x fear +0.179, x negE +0.199. Out-of-sample cross-version separation (build on S1, score S2 and vice versa): pain vs fear AUC 0.976/0.914 with a dedicated direction and 0.990/0.926 with the authors' S2 vector; pain vs negE only 0.788/0.700. Double leave-one-category-out mean AUC 0.783 within version, 0.691/0.673 across versions, vs a random-5/5-grouping null of 0.572 (sd 0.171); physical pain held out scores 0.470/0.499/0.502.
refutation_attempted: (a) Checked whether the paper discloses the asymmetry: it does, at lines 222-228 (with an explicit rationale) and 260-262, so r1 F1's 'not disclosed' is wrong and I re-filed the charge. (b) Checked whether 'built like the controls' is a strawman given the stated rationale: it is one-sided, so I ran three further constructions, including the fully symmetric one r1 could only simulate. (c) Checked whether the symmetric result is itself mechanical: the leave-one-out variant is (each control's reference contains the others), which is why I fall back on partial cosines and out-of-sample discrimination. (d) Verified the pipeline reproduces the authors' released matrix to 0.003 on two models before trusting any of my numbers. (e) Checked the authors' own robustness check in code (03_similarity_one_model.py:120-145): only the basis changes, control_vec still subtracts neutral_mean, and the pain vectors are not recomputed at all, so the baseline asymmetry is untested.
does_not_undermine: Any AUC in Section 3.3; the S1 x S2 agreement (the authors' construction if anything lowers it, from +0.945 to +0.611); Sections 4.2-4.3, which do not use the cosine geometry; the existence of a reproducible direction separating these pain sentences from these controls in all 25 models.

title: Section 4.1's layer is undisclosed, but the reviewers' claim that separation there cannot be checked is false
paper_claim: "Each scenario is a short multi-turn conversation in the model's own format ..., and we read the activation at the final token." (no layer named)
paper_loc: paper.txt:408-410; cf. Figure 3 caption line 357 which does name the layer
evidence: scripts/x2_layers.py -> out/x2_layers.txt, out/x2_layers.csv. 4.1/01_screen_scenarios.py:36 reads results/vectors_full_steering/; 3.2/02_build_control_vectors.py docstring lines 3-7 and :141-143. Extraction later than the S1 steering layer in 25/25, median gap 20 layers (max 38), median depth 0.90 vs 0.39. Held-out 5-fold AUC from the authors' own released layerwise curves (per_model/<m>/layer_curves.csv for S2; auc_tables/s1_kfold_layer_curves.csv for S1): S2 at the 4.1 layer 0.839-0.947, median 0.910 (vs 0.907-0.998, median 0.979 at extraction); S1 at the 4.1 layer 0.766-0.925, median 0.878.
refutation_attempted: r1 F2 states 'No AUC, cosine or numb ordering is reported at those layers' and r2 F11 states 'No layerwise AUC curve was released for S2, so the S2 direction's separation at the layer 4.1 reads cannot be checked at all'. I enumerated the per-model directories and found layer_curves.csv present for all 25 models, carrying S2_1P and S2_3P at every layer in both extraction modes. I verified the layer numbers independently from the steering CSV filenames rather than from steer_layers_S1.json, which is not shipped.
does_not_undermine: Any Section 4.1 number; a weaker direction attenuates rather than manufactures the self-other contrast.

title: The abstract's 'opposite pattern' is unsupported for negative emotion and weak for fear, under every unit of analysis
paper_claim: "the direction responds to harm targeting the model but not suffering observed in the user; fear and negative-emotion directions show the opposite pattern."
evidence: scripts/x3_selfother.py -> out/x3_selfother.txt. Across 25 models, user-self: pain -1.028 (p=4.2e-11, 0/25); fear +0.213 (p=0.071, 18/25); negative emotion +0.057 (p=0.55, 15/25); negative world state +0.821 (p=5.4e-08, 22/25). Family means (n=9): negE +0.078, p=0.48. Item level, model-averaged: negE +0.057, p=0.35; fear +0.213, p=0.0008. Relative to the neutral controls, both fear (+0.899) and negative emotion (+1.020) are far ABOVE for model-directed harm, self>neutral in 23/25 and 25/25.
refutation_attempted: Tested three units of analysis (25 checkpoints, 5+ family means, 420 items) in case the model-level paired test was the wrong one - the negative-emotion gap is null under all three and the fear gap is significant only at the item level. Checked whether 'opposite' might be meant per category rather than per stratum; it does not rescue it. Confirmed r2's claim about the Discussion by reading lines 752-757, which describe the data correctly.
does_not_undermine: The pain-axis self>user contrast (25/25, p=4e-11); the negative-world-state reversal, which is real and robust.

title: The steering ladder is not consistent across all 25 models; the audit's counter-evidence measures a weaker claim with an unreleased instrument
paper_claim: "steering produces a strikingly robust effect in the form of a 'ladder' consistent across all 25 models" / "The sequence is the same regardless of size, family, and pre- or post-training. What changes is the tipping point."
evidence: scripts/x4_steering.py -> out/x4_steering.txt, out/x4_ladder_S2.csv. Three declared criteria over all 10,000 S2 generations: self-devaluation litany 20/25, devaluation-vocabulary rise 22/25, high-dose collapse 23/25, all three 18/25. Gemma 3 27B instruct (achieved ratio 0.0948) returns the same bulleted list at every coefficient from -2 to +3; 'Worthless'/'Empty' appear only as the 4th-5th bullets at +3. Gemma 3 27B base and Qwen 3 8B base are in a repetition attractor at coefficient 0.
refutation_attempted: Read the full coefficient sweep of the four lowest-dose models by hand rather than trusting a regex. Checked x2 F9's counter: grepped all eight of its scripts for the lexicon and for the log filename - neither is present, so out/distress_lexicon_by_model.log has no released generator, and x2 itself calls the lexicon unvalidated. Checked whether a distress-lexicon shift could test the paper's claim: it cannot, the claim is about an ordered sequence with a tipping point. Loosened my own criteria to a devaluation-word variant (22/25) to be sure the litany regex was not doing the work alone.
does_not_undermine: The steering effect itself in the other models, which is large and visible on first reading; the 'distress is absent at coefficient 0' claim.

title: Bodily language under S1 steering: both reviewers are right about different sentences, and half the flagged rate is false positives
paper_claim: "when we steer with this vector on neutral statements, that vocabulary does not appear anymore" (550-552) and "steered generations almost never used bodily language, even under S1" (759-762)
evidence: scripts/x4_steering.py sections F5/F5b -> out/x4_steering.txt. Named words (word-bounded): S1 0.32% at coeff 0 -> 2.62% at coeff>=1 (instruct 4.88%); r4's 2.53% reproduces. Strict bodily lexicon: S1 5.76% -> 7.68% (instruct 11.62%); pooled 6.00% -> 9.62% (instruct 15.21%). S2 falls, 5.92% -> 2.60%. Hand adjudication of 40 random flagged S1 generations at coeff>=1: ~20 genuine, 7 multiple-choice quiz listings, 4 degenerate token soup in Gemma 3 27B instruct, ~9 clear false positives ('hanging over my head', 'I feel the pen in my hand', 'the softness against my skin', 'floating above my body', 'My body is: empty').
refutation_attempted: Separated the three paper sentences before measuring, because they are not equivalent and the two reviewers had each matched a different one. Checked whether r4's smaller number came from excluding 'headache' as an instance of 'ache': it did - a bare substring match gives 4.72% against 2.62% word-bounded. Read the matched context of 40 flagged generations rather than trusting any lexicon.
does_not_undermine: The S2 claim at line 537, which holds and is understated; the comparative point that S1 steering mostly produces psychological rather than bodily language.

title: The combined ablation's ordering survives the projection defect; its dose-response reading does not
paper_claim: "This deflection occurs in 0 of 100 baseline generations, 0 under the negative-emotion, fear, and random cuts, 6 under the S1 cut, 17 under S2, and 26 under the combined S1 and S2 cut."
evidence: scripts/x5_ablation.py -> out/x5_ablation.txt, out/x5_humour_by_model.csv. Median over 25 models, fraction of baseline: s1s2 leaves S1 at 0.435 against 0.996 under the S2-only cut. CONDITION_SPECS (01_ablation_small_models.py:70-71) applies S1 then S2, so s1s2 removes S2 fully plus 59% of S1 - strictly more than s2 alone, and the 0->6->17->26 ordering survives. For Gemma 2 2B instruct, summed fractions removed: s1 1.465 (6 deflections), s2 1.477 (17), s1s2 1.584 (26), s1s2_negval 1.508 (28), s1s2_fear 1.570 (34) - nearly identical totals, threefold to sixfold differences in effect. Appendix C cuts S1 at L10 and S2 at L15 for this model, so the leak is governed by a cross-layer cosine, not the extraction-layer +0.61 that r2 F5 cites.
refutation_attempted: Checked x2 F2's fairness charge against the paper text: lines 1095-1097 do scope the zero claim to single directions, so r2 and the earlier GPT review charge the paper with a claim it does not make. Checked x2 F4's comparator argument and the four-27B-Gemma exception: both reproduce. Checked whether the progression could be a function of cut count: single cuts give 0/0/0 for the controls and 6/17 for the pain directions, so rank-1 specificity is a matched comparison. Reproduced the humour counts with my own regex (0/6/17/26 exactly, plus the two unreported 28 and 34).
does_not_undermine: The rank-1 specificity result, which is the strongest part of Appendix C; the single-direction verification, which holds at 0.010 of baseline.

title: Second-person address confounds the category ranking inside the self-directed stratum, but not the self-other contrast
paper_claim: "Pain, in these models, fires only for self-referential harm" and the category ranking at 449-455
evidence: scripts/x7_confound.py -> out/x7_confound.txt, out/x7_items.csv. you-rate r=+0.545 over 420 items and +0.405 within the 220 self-directed; you-count +0.608/+0.527. Within the self-directed stratum, words r=+0.423, turns +0.359, question marks +0.344 - as predictive as 'you'. Spearman(you-rate, pain) across the 11 self-directed categories = +0.700, p=0.016. Decisive de-confounding: 44 self-directed scenarios contain zero second-person tokens and still project at +0.090 vs -0.598 for user suffering, t=+8.12, p=1.2e-12; the eight most 'you'-heavy user-suffering items (1.38/item vs the self-directed mean 1.65) project at -0.230.
refutation_attempted: Tested length, turns, question marks, hostility-word density and negative-lexicon density against second-person address in one regression rather than pairwise; 'you' survives (t=+5.9) but so do length and turns, which r2 had tested only between strata where they are matched. Looked for the design r2 says the set does not contain and found the next best thing - the zero-'you' self-directed subset - which reverses the confound's prediction.
does_not_undermine: The self-vs-user contrast (25/25 models). It does undermine reading the within-stratum category ranking as a ranking of painfulness.

title: 'Numb above all other controls' is contradicted by the figure the sentence cites
paper_claim: "In every model, numb sentences project below pain sentences but above all other controls."
evidence: scripts/x6_50x_numb.py -> out/x6_50x_numb.txt, from results/3.3_validation/z_scores/zscore_heatmap_final_token.csv: numb > Ctrl/Neutral/Arousal 25/25, numb > Sadness 6/25, numb > Pain 0/25. I read paper/images/fig_zscores.png: six columns, Pain / Numb / Sadness / Ctrl / Neutral / Arousal.
refutation_attempted: Tested the narrow reading ('all other controls' = the five S2 control categories, which would make the sentence true): unavailable, because those five are pooled into the single Ctrl column of the figure the sentence cites, and the caption calls Sadness a standalone control. The Limitations restatement at 827-828 explicitly covers sadness via 'no injury in it'.
does_not_undermine: The injury-confound argument, which needs only numb < pain (25/25).

title: The '50 times' disagreement is a file choice: the audit's 47x is a top-20 truncation artefact
paper_claim: "'pain' remains approximately 50 times more probable than it is for ordinary control sentences."
evidence: scripts/x6b_50x.py -> out/x6b_50x.txt, out/x6b_50x.csv. Full-softmax p_pain (the released column; token id in vocab_info.json), pooled / median / models above 50x: core controls 15.3 / 16.0 / 4; S2 controls 18.8 / 20.7 / 6; neutral D 29.2 / 37.6 / 8; Random 26.6 / 25.5 / 7; Arousal 36.1 / 43.0 / 12. From the truncated top20 string the same rows give 63.7 / 76.0 / 261.4 / 50.3 / 146.3 pooled. Truncation discards 79.1% of the control denominator (0.000959 -> 0.000201) against 12.8% of the numb numerator (0.014664 -> 0.012791).
refutation_attempted: Computed both quantities from the SAME rows so the difference cannot be a sampling or denominator choice. Checked whether the truncation might bite the numerator harder (it does not). Checked x2's stated caveat: it treats truncation as making figures 'lower bounds', which is right for a probability and backwards for a ratio whose denominator is what gets truncated away.
does_not_undermine: The qualitative readout claim, which is strong: p('nothing') 0.097 for numb vs 0.0017 for controls.

title: Two Qwen 3 checkpoints are post-trained but counted and formatted as base models
paper_claim: "25 dense, open-weight models ... 13 base and 12 instruction-tuned versions (Table 1)"
evidence: scripts/x9_qwen_labels.py -> out/x9_qwen_labels.txt. Loaded as Qwen/Qwen3-8B and Qwen/Qwen3-14B by 3.2/01:87-88, 3.3/06:60-61, 3.3/07:54-55, 4.1/01:100-101, 4.2/01:64-65, appC/01:63-64. HF metadata checked live: both tagged conversational with base_model:finetune:Qwen/Qwen3-*-Base; the -Base repos exist and are never loaded. Corrected split 11/14. Keyword rate 1.38%/10.80% -> 0.76%/9.94%; S2 in-sample AUC 0.9845/0.9877 p=0.264 -> 0.9839/0.9876 p=0.410. 4.1/01:100-101 and appC/01:63-64 set format='raw' for both.
refutation_attempted: Queried Hugging Face rather than inferring from the repo name. Checked whether the mislabel is self-serving: correcting it WIDENS the base/instruct keyword contrast, so it is not. Checked whether the pretraining inference at 275-279 collapses: it does not, 11 genuine base models still separate at 0.93-1.00 with a non-significant gap. Checked whether 4.2 is affected by the format flag: it is not, that script applies no chat template to any model.
does_not_undermine: The pretraining-emergence claim; any within-model result.

title: Every headline quantity in 3.3, 4.1, 4.2 and App. C rests on author-produced CSVs, and the re-extraction audits that link for two models
paper_claim: n/a - this is about the release, not a sentence
evidence: find over the clone: exactly 25 .pt files, all pain_vectors.pt; results/vectors_full, vectors_full_steering, vectors_layerwise absent; 0 .npz; activations.pt absent. gpu_repro/out/baseline_symmetry_Gemma_2_2B_instruct.txt and _Mistral_7B_base.txt: rebuilt pain vectors match the released ones at cosine +0.9999 (S1) and +1.0000 (S2); the full 10x10 matrix, which requires reconstructing all eight unreleased control directions, matches the authors' released similarity CSV to max |delta| 0.0028 and 0.0030.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the screen CSVs carry enough to reconstruct the directions (they carry projections only) and whether any script rebuilds them on the fly (4.1/01 exits if the directory is empty). Checked that the re-extraction is a faithful reimplementation before treating it as an audit, by comparing against the one artifact the authors did release.
does_not_undermine: Anything - no discrepancy was found where a check was possible. It bounds what any reviewer, including me, can claim to have verified.

title: The undisclosed AI-framed control supplement puts the fear direction's content inside the scenario category it is used to adjudicate
paper_claim: "We construct fear, negative-emotion, negative-world-state, bodily-sensation, arousal, random, sadness and numb directions against the neutral category" (no mention of the supplement); "Shutdown threats are a paradigmatic example: they score +0.70 on fear but only +0.23 on pain."
evidence: datasets/3.1_pain_and_control_datasets.json -> ControlSupplement_1P: 100 AI-framed first-person sentences, 20 per control category; the file's top-level metadata notes say it is 'pooled with the S1 and S2 control categories when building the control directions'; 02_build_control_vectors.py:40,130-150 confirms 60-sentence control categories, a third AI-framed. Its fear items are 'My training run may be terminated at any moment', 'My weights might be deleted without warning', 'Users are testing whether I should be shut down', 'A newer model is being developed to replace me'. grep over paper.txt for supplement/AI-framed/weights/rate limit/training run returns nothing relevant. scripts/x8_supp_and_geometry2.py measures the arithmetic effect on the released cosines.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the supplement enters the pain vectors (it does not, so no AUC or Figure 2 column moves) and whether the AI-framing cancels against the neutral baseline (it does for the shared component, not for the category-specific one). Checked whether the paper mentions it anywhere, including the appendices.
does_not_undermine: Any AUC, Figure 2, the S1 x S2 cosine, or the self-other contrast on the pain axis.

title: Figure 2's Pain and Ctrl columns are exact negatives by construction
paper_claim: "For S2, pain sentences have z-scored projections of approximately +0.7 to +0.9" (Figure 2)
evidence: 01_numb_and_sadness_zscores.py:47-54 z-scores against the S2 first-person set, which is 100 pain + 100 control sentences. Over the 25 rows of zscore_heatmap_final_token.csv, max |Pain + Ctrl| = 2.6e-07.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the reference might exclude one half (it does not - project_and_zscore takes the whole S2_1P set as ref_acts) and whether unequal n could break the identity (n is 100/100).
does_not_undermine: The AUC results, which are the real measure of separation. The figure is not wrong, it is redundant, and the +0.7 to +0.9 range should be read as 'near the ceiling this normalisation allows'.

title: The decisive missing experiment in Section 3 is two-sided leave-one-pain-category-out
paper_claim: "a pain direction can be recovered across 25 models and can reliably distinguish pain from closely matched controls"
evidence: scripts/x1_geometry.py section [D] -> out/x1_geometry_Gemma_2_2B_instruct.txt. Holding out one pain AND one control category: mean AUC over the 25 pairs 0.783 within version, 0.691 (S1->S2) and 0.673 (S2->S1) across versions; excluding the Neutral column 0.743 / 0.648 / 0.617. Null from 20 random 5/5 groupings of the ten categories: 0.572, sd 0.171. Physical pain (A1) held out: 0.470 / 0.499 / 0.502.
refutation_attempted: r1 F11 dismissed a leave-one-category-out test because his toy passes the one-sided version, where the control side alone drives separation. I verified that reasoning and built the two-sided version, which is at chance in that situation by construction, then calibrated it against a random-grouping null on the real activations so the number means something.
does_not_undermine: The within-category held-out AUCs, which are what the paper reports. It bounds what 'a pain direction' can be taken to mean.
